name: chat
purpose: A conversation view for an AI assistant or for people: user, assistant, system, and tool messages with avatars and timestamps (day separators name holidays and non-working days from a business calendar), assistant replies streamed from a host-supplied AsyncIterable<string> or ReadableStream<string> with Stop and Retry, a typing indicator, per-message errors, attachments as file chips, suggestion chips, copy and feedback actions, and auto-scroll that pauses while the user reads earlier messages (with a Jump to latest button). Text renders as plain text or as a safe Markdown subset, never as HTML from the model. The composer is a Prompt Input.
whenToUse: An assistant or copilot panel that streams answers from a language model.
Support or team conversations with people (typing indicator, attachments).
Showing a transcript of a conversation, read-only (composer off).
whenNotToUse: A single question and answer: use a form with Prompt Input or Textarea and show the result.
Notifications or activity feeds: use a list or Toast.
Comments attached to records with threading: build on a list; Chat is linear.
states: reading earlier messages (Jump to latest shown)
responsive: Fills the height the host gives it: the log scrolls and the composer stays at the bottom. Bubbles take at most 48rem; on narrow screens they use the full width. Actions are always visible on touch screens.
rtl: User messages sit on the left in right-to-left layouts; logical properties throughout. Code blocks keep left-to-right order.
theme: Component tokens chat-user-bg/-fg (color-selected roles), chat-assistant-bg/-fg (sunken surface and text), chat-code-bg, and chat-bubble-radius, all in the contrast gate. Forced-colors mode outlines bubbles with CanvasText. The typing dots stop animating for reduced motion and animation 'none'.
timezone: Times and day separators use the configured timezone (common config or the timezone option), never the machine's zone; messages carry Instants.
security: Message text is never parsed as HTML: plain text uses textContent, and Markdown is parsed into a fixed set of elements whose text is set with textContent. Links render only for http(s) and scheme-less URLs (isSafeHref) and open with rel=noopener noreferrer nofollow; unsafe links keep only their label. Avatar images go through the Avatar URL policy. Error details from the stream are not shown (a generic or host-supplied message is).
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry. Streams are read only while a message is streaming and are cancelled on Stop or destroy. Copy writes to the clipboard only when the user activates a copy button.

budgets.metric: Streaming repaint of a 5,000-character Markdown reply
budgets.budget: < 8 ms per repaint (repaints are batched to at most one per 40 ms)

performance.testedScale: 10,000 messages in the model with 200 in the DOM (maxRenderedMessages); replies up to 200,000 characters as Markdown, longer as plain text.

limitations: The DOM keeps at most maxRenderedMessages messages (default 200); earlier ones are added back in steps by 'Show earlier messages'. The list is not virtualized.
The Markdown subset has no tables, images, task lists, or HTML; nested lists follow indentation of two or more spaces.
Code blocks are shown as text without syntax highlighting.
Announcements read the first 300 characters of a finished reply.
unsupported: Threaded replies or message editing (the host can replace messages with addMessage or update).
Reading attachments: the host opens them on aui-attachment-open.
antiPatterns: Passing model output as HTML into a custom renderer next to the chat: use the Markdown format.
Announcing every streamed token through your own live region.
Giving the host element no height: the log then grows with the page and auto-scroll has nothing to scroll.
